description:
Wintergreen (Gaultheria procumbens) is a plant whose concentrated essential oil is extremely dangerous to cats. This oil can be found in products like muscle rubs, liniments, and some scented items. Cats must not ingest wintergreen oil or have it applied to their skin or fur.

The toxic compound is methyl salicylate, which is chemically similar to aspirin. Cats lack the specific liver enzymes needed to process salicylates effectively. This means the toxin can quickly build up in their system to poisonous levels, even from what might seem like a small exposure. Absorption through the skin is a major risk, especially if a cat licks the oil off while grooming.

Wintergreen poisoning is a medical emergency. Symptoms can include vomiting, severe weakness, difficulty breathing, tremors, seizures, and internal organ failure. If you suspect your cat has been exposed to any product containing wintergreen oil, do not wait for symptoms to appear. Please contact a veterinarian or an emergency animal hospital immediately.
name: Wintergreen
safetyNotes: Main hazard: Methyl salicylate in wintergreen oil is processed very slowly by cats and can build up to dangerous levels.
Symptoms: Drooling, vomiting, weakness, tremors, labored breathing, stomach bleeding, seizures, collapse, or organ injury.
Highest-risk forms: Essential oil, muscle rubs, liniments, oral care products, and any oil left on the fur.
Action: Never use wintergreen products on cats; call a vet or poison helpline immediately after any oil exposure.

symptoms.name: Shaking, tremoring, and walking as if they are drunk (ataxia)
Difficulty breathing or breathing with the mouth open
Sore or red skin, and chemical burns
Liver failure, seizures, collapse, and death
